doc.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Listening to 'Margie' and talking gospel and blues pianists
summary: Rowe plays a track with Dan Barrett; Ingham talks about gospel and blues pianists, Ray Bryant, and Mahalia Jackson's pianist.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: I wanted to play one thing for you before you go.
“Margie.” That’s Dan Barrett and that’s me. Oh yeah.
This caught my ear because I hear, in the background, he’s playing some nice blues.
Oh, I love that. I love those piano players. Yeah I love that music. Gospel music. I’m crazy about it. Oh the music of those churches, the blues thing. Jay McShann.

Thank you. One of my favorite piano players, Ray Bryant, he used to do that stuff. His sister was a wonderful, I believe, Gospel player, played in church, a pianist. And you ever heard that piano player with Mahalia Jackson? Mildred Falls? You ever seen that Mahalia Jackson “Jazz on a Summer’s Day?”

And when they do that, “Didn’t It Rain” that’s rocking, I mean that swings like Basie and everything. I mean it’s just incredible. It’s just I think an organ and a piano, and I think that’s about it. And then there’s Mahalia’s thing. It’s just incredible.
And she’s got a tambourine or something. Oh, yeah, it’s glorious.
